comparator.name: Bachelor Natuurwetenschap en Innovatiemanagement
comparator.route: Energy & Transport domain with Innovation & Business Management learning line
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from Utrecht University's current official prospective-student overview and study-programme pages plus the current official student major page. The major page states that every course carries 7.5 EC unless otherwise indicated and fixes the 135-EC major as 75 EC of ten common compulsory courses, one complete 30-EC domain of four courses, a 15-EC bachelor thesis in that domain, and one complete 15-EC learning line of two courses. The overview and programme page independently fix the profiling space at 45 EC (six courses), giving 135 + 45 = 180 EC. The chosen route is the first-listed Energy & Transport domain (Science of Energy Technologies; Introduction to Energy and Material Analysis; Applied Thermodynamics & Energy Conversions; Management van Energie- en Transportinnovaties; 15-EC Bachelorthesis E&T) together with the first-listed Innovation & Business Management learning line (Organisation Theories; Innovation Strategies of Firms and Entrepreneurs). Official published order is used only as a neutral, UCR-independent tie-break among equally formal options. The current official pages therefore establish a complete and internally consistent 180-EC pathway before any UCR course is considered.

routeSelection.route: Energy & Transport domain with Innovation & Business Management learning line
routeSelection.basis: The current official major page requires one 30-EC substantive domain and one 15-EC learning line. Energy & Transport is the first-listed of the two equally formal domains, and Innovation & Business Management is the first-listed of the three equally formal learning lines. No target-specific evidence privileges a different combination, so official published order is used as a neutral tie-break. This route was fixed independently of UCR fit.

core: Combining natural science with innovation management across science, business and government
Turning scientific discoveries into useful innovations and understanding why technologies succeed or fail
Entrepreneurship, firm strategy and the financing of innovative technologies
Project-based innovation work with societal partners
Research design, statistics and evaluation methods for innovation studies
Economics, organisation theory and management of innovation
Public policy, regulation, societal transitions and social consequences of technological change
Mathematics, systems analysis and digital/data foundations for innovation analysis
Financing and commercial assessment of emerging technologies
Ethical and societal assessment of new technologies
adjacent: Energy and transport innovation, energy technologies, materials and conversions, renewable systems and clean mobility
Life-science and medical innovation, molecular and human biology, medicines and new medical technologies
questions: Illustrative current innovation cases used by the programme (care robots, patenting a medicine, neighbourhood batteries, offshore wind, heat pumps and DNA modification)
Possible graduate directions in innovation research, consultancy, policy, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, sustainability and emerging-technology management

alternatives.label: Science, Technology and Innovation Management
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR's business/entrepreneurship/finance cluster (7 of 24: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Research Methods & Statistics, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance, Introduction to Economics), a mathematics/data/programming cluster (4 of 24: Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science), an organisational-behaviour and ethics cluster (2 of 24: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Ethics), an energy/sustainability cluster (4 of 24: Sustainability Essentials I, Climate Change, Governance of Sustainability, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy) and a life-science/health cluster (5 of 24: Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity), plus Dynamic Earth and Personal & Professional Development. The label names technology innovation management first for the dominant business/methods/strategy backbone that runs through every semester, and energy and life sciences second because the curriculum deliberately balances UCR's sustainability offerings against its biomedical/life-science offerings in roughly equal measure, reproducing the comparator's own parallel Year-1/Year-2 innovation-project structure (medicines and energy in Year 1; diagnostics/health and the energy transition in Year 2) and its own two published career tracks (Energy & Sustainability; Life & Health) rather than favouring either domain.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Utrecht's Natuurwetenschap en Innovatiemanagement: an interdisciplinary core in entrepreneurship, economics, organisation, research methods, statistics, mathematics, programming, data analysis and technology ethics, balanced across environmental sustainability and biomedical/life-science applications. It reproduces the programme-wide academic identity and both named application domains as closely as UCR's catalogue permits, while preserving the comparator's 45-EC profiling space without inventing an elective package.
progression: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for HCBLIFE213, HCBBIOM311, HCBBIOM313 and HCBBIOM312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENENTR212 (semester 2), BENENTR311 and BENBUSI312 (semester 6), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 5) and BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally require it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISMATH211 (semester 3), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Programming, Sustainability Essentials I, Research Methods & Statistics) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (Pharmacology, Governance of Sustainability, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Sustainable Energy and Transport Innovation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum replaces the closest match's life-science/health cluster with a deeper sustainability/energy cluster (9 of 24: Sustainability Essentials I, Sustainability Essentials II, Climate Change, Governance of Sustainability, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, Renewable System Design, Earth's Resources, R3: Recycling Recovery Remediation, Earth Observation), while retaining the identical shared business/methods/ethics core (14 of 24) that all three alternatives share. The label names sustainable energy innovation first for the dominant, now much deeper sustainability-cluster content, and the energy transition second for the governance, renewable-system-design and resource-economics content that together organise this alternative's distinctive academic priorities.

It keeps the shared innovation-management, economics, methods and ethics core while replacing the balanced route's life-science breadth with UCR's deepest available study of renewable systems, energy and materials, environmental monitoring, sustainability governance and transitions.

alternatives.distinctness: VU's Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation names 'sustainable energy innovation' and 'the energy transition for companies and governments' as two of its own generator-eligible programme-interest rows (5287, 5302), independently corroborated by the current official Toekomst page naming 'Energy & Sustainability' as one of only two published career tracks (alongside 'Life & Health') and by the programme's own OER learning outcomes naming 'energie- en levenswetenschappen' as its twin application domains. The closest match reproduces the shared business/methods/ethics core together with an even balance of UCR's sustainability and life-science offerings, standing in for the comparator's own parallel Year-1/Year-2 energy-and-health project structure. This alternative instead retains the identical shared business/methods/ethics core (14 of 24 courses) but replaces the closest match's five life-science/health courses with five new UCR sustainability/energy courses (Sustainability Essentials II, Renewable System Design, Earth's Resources, R3: Recycling Recovery Remediation, Earth Observation), for a total of nine energy/sustainability courses concentrating the programme on how technology and governance drive the energy transition. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a balanced dual-domain generalist programme to a single-domain energy concentration, and the two alternatives share 19 of 24 courses while differing in 5 of 24 each way (37.5 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

alternatives.distinctness: VU's Bachelor Science, Business & Innovation names 'life-science and health innovation' as one of its own generator-eligible programme-interest rows (5288), independently corroborated by the current official Toekomst page naming 'Life & Health' as one of only two published career tracks (alongside 'Energy & Sustainability') and by the programme's own OER learning outcomes naming 'energie- en levenswetenschappen' as its twin application domains, and by support rows on chemistry/biochemistry/molecules-to-medicines (5294) and clinical diagnostics and imaging (5300). The closest match reproduces the shared business/methods/ethics core together with an even balance of UCR's sustainability and life-science offerings. This alternative instead retains the identical shared business/methods/ethics core (14 of 24 courses) but replaces the closest match's four energy/sustainability courses with five new UCR life-science courses (Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Medical & Health Psychology), for a total of ten life-science/health courses concentrating the programme on the biological and human dimensions of medical innovation. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from a balanced dual-domain generalist programme to a single-domain health/life-science concentration, and this alternative differs from the closest match in 5 of 24 courses each way (37.5 EC) and from the energy alternative in 10 of 24 courses each way (75 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum in both comparisons.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-wide generator-eligible interests: useful innovation, the combination of natural science and innovation management, technology success and failure, innovation economics and organisations, public policy and regulation, ethics, finance, collaboration across science/business/government, societal challenges, social consequences, entrepreneurship and innovation strategy, and sustainable-system transitions (15566-15571 and 15576-15583). These define the shared science-and-innovation-management identity rather than separate routes. The remaining generator-eligible evidence forms two coherent substantive directions: Energy & Transport (15572, 15573 and the stable direction 15584) and Life-Science & Medical Innovation (15574, 15575 and the stable direction 15585). Each passes the evidence, organising-logic, distinctness and mechanical-feasibility gates. The UCR energy route replaces five courses (37.5 EC) from the closest schedule; the life-science route also replaces five courses (37.5 EC), and the two focused routes differ by ten courses (75 EC). All three schedules contain 24 distinct 7.5-EC courses and at least six level-300 courses. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore included and no generator-eligible evidence remains unassigned.

notes.text: Utrecht's programme combines innovation studies with a selected natural-science application domain and a structured innovation-management major. UCR can assemble closely related business, entrepreneurship, data, sustainability and biomedical coursework, but does not offer a named innovation-management major; these are interdisciplinary UCR pathways through related fields rather than course-for-course replicas.

The selected official comparator route includes dedicated energy-technology science, energy/material analysis, applied thermodynamics and energy conversions, a domain-specific management course and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. UCR offers adjacent sustainability, environment and renewable-systems courses, but no physics/thermodynamics course and no scheduled course equivalent to the thesis. The life-science alternative similarly uses UCR's biomedical courses without claiming to reproduce Utrecht's formal life-science domain package.
